stops.note: a padded tunic, possibly named from Jacques, the nickname for a French peasant, as in the Jacquerie revolt of 1358; an Arabic source has also been proposed
via its Middle French diminutive jaquet, a short close-fitting coat; later extended to covers, like potatoes baked 'in their jackets' and paper dust jackets on books from the 1890s

current_meaning: a short coat; an outer covering
